title: Same Answer, Different Reasons: Trace-Level Divergence in Multilingual Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.29092v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multilingual large language models are increasingly deployed in settings where visible reasoning traces support verification, education, and safety auditing, yet standard evaluations typically measure only final-answer agreement or holistic response similarity. As a result, they establish outcome consistency without determining whether users across languages receive comparable supporting evidence. We introduce a trace-level divergence framework that compares visible reasoning traces as structured sequences, decomposing agreement into structural similarity, order consistency, and holistic similarity, with pair-specific calibration to enable comparison across languages. Across three reasoning benchmarks, seven languages, and six frontier LLMs, the natural baseline---embedding each whole response and comparing the two by cosine---systematically overstates agreement: $52.1\%$--$67.3\%$ of examples in the top quartile of holistic similarity

translated_title: 相同的答案，不同的理由：多语言大语言模型中的推理轨迹级分歧
translated_abstract: 多语言大语言模型越来越多地被部署在可见推理轨迹能够支持验证、教育和安全审计的场景中，然而标准评估通常只衡量最终答案的一致性或整体响应的相似性。因此，这些评估只能建立结果层面的一致性，而无法确定不同语言的用户是否获得了可比性的支持证据。我们提出了一个轨迹级分歧框架，将可见的推理轨迹作为结构化序列进行比较，把一致性分解为结构相似性、顺序一致性和整体相似性三个维度，并采用针对特定语言对的校准方法以实现跨语言比较。在三个推理基准、七种语言和六个前沿大语言模型的实验中，自然的基线方法——对整个响应进行嵌入并通过余弦相似度进行比较——系统性地高估了一致性：在整体相似度最高四分位数的样本中，有 $52.1\%$–$67.3\%$ 的样本
tldr: 该论文提出一个轨迹级分歧框架，将多语言大语言模型的可见推理轨迹作为结构化序列分解为结构相似性、顺序一致性和整体相似性进行比较，发现标准的整体嵌入余弦比较方法会系统性高估跨语言的推理一致性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a trace-level divergence framework that compares visible reasoning traces as structured sequences—decomposing agreement into structural similarity, order consistency, and holistic similarity—showing that standard whole-response embedding comparison systematically overstates cross-lingual reasoning consistency in multilingual LLMs.
